content: HOT-17, chemically known as 2,5-dimethoxy-4-(β-isobutylthio)-N-hydroxyphenethylamine, is a psychedelic compound belonging to the phenethylamine class, specifically the 2C family. It was likely first synthesized by the chemist Alexander Shulgin and documented in his book PIHKAL (Phenethylamines I Have Known and Loved). The complete chemical name of HOT-17 is 2-[4-(2-isobutylthio)-2,5-dimethoxyphenyl]-N-hydroxyethanamine. Its molecular structure shares similarities with 2C-T-17 and other compounds in the HOTseries, particularly HOT-2 and HOT-7, which are closely related analogs. The effective dosage range for HOT-17 is generally between 70 and 120 milligrams. The psychoactive effects typically last for a duration of approximately 12 to 18 hours, as described by Shulgin. The substance is known to induce perceptual distortions related to time and general psychedelic effects. Notably, it is reported to produce minimal to no physical discomfort or body load during its effects.
